sections.heading: Understanding Arabic Script Fundamentals
paragraphs: Arabic is written right-to-left, and most letters connect to those around them, changing their shape depending on whether they appear at the start, middle or end of a word.
The online keyboard applies these joining rules automatically, producing the correct contextual forms that a native reader expects.
Diacritics such as fatha, kasra and damma can be added where precision of vowel sounds matters, such as in religious texts or beginner learning materials.
Because Arabic omits short vowels in everyday writing, the tool focuses on providing accurate standalone letters and contextual shaping without requiring you to manage connections yourself.
